questions.text: How does the source define pneumonia?

answers.text: A lower respiratory tract infection that inflames the alveoli
A chronic genetic disorder of chloride transport
A permanent enlargement of airspaces beyond terminal bronchioles
A mean pulmonary artery pressure above 25 mmHg

questions.text: Which statement best distinguishes lobar pneumonia from bronchopneumonia?

answers.text: Lobar pneumonia affects an entire lobe or lung; bronchopneumonia has patchy foci of consolidation
Lobar pneumonia is always viral; bronchopneumonia is always fungal
Lobar pneumonia is latent; bronchopneumonia is never infectious
Lobar pneumonia is obstructive; bronchopneumonia is restrictive

questions.text: Which patient is in a pneumonia risk group listed in the source?

answers.text: A smoker older than 65
A patient with no respiratory history and no exposures
A patient with normal immunity and no infections
A patient whose only finding is mild scoliosis

questions.text: Which organism is listed as a typical acute community-acquired pneumonia pathogen?

answers.text: Streptococcus pneumoniae
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Histoplasma capsulatum
Pneumocystis jiroveci

questions.text: Which history matches health care-associated pneumonia (HCAP) in the source?

answers.text: Hospitalized in acute care for 2 or more days within the last 90 days
Intubated for less than 12 hours with no symptoms
No health care exposure and symptoms beginning at home
Only a positive PPD without symptoms
More than 48 hours after hospital admission, after CAP is ruled out
Within minutes of bronchodilator therapy
Only after discharge from a long-term care facility
Only after a positive IGRA test

questions.text: Ventilator-associated pneumonia is defined by infection developing:

answers.text: More than 48-72 hours after intubation
Before endotracheal intubation
Only during spontaneous breathing without an airway
Only months to years after exposure

questions.text: Which mechanism is listed as a pneumonia pathogenesis route?

answers.text: Aspiration from the oropharynx during sleep or impaired gag reflex
Increased pulmonary artery pressure alone
Small unstable pharyngeal airway during sleep only
A thymus antibody destroying acetylcholine receptors

questions.text: A patient reports sudden sharp chest pain when inhaling and exhaling. Which pneumonia sign does this match?

answers.text: Pleuritic chest pain
Orthopnea from emphysema
Pulsus paradoxus
Diplopia

questions.text: Which lab finding category is listed for pneumonia diagnosis?

answers.text: ABG showing low oxygenation values
Sweat chloride greater than 60 mEq/L only
AHI greater than 30 events/hr
Mean pulmonary artery pressure greater than 25 mmHg

questions.text: What is the purpose of sputum sensitivity testing?

answers.text: To determine whether a specific antibiotic or antifungal is likely to stop organism growth
To calculate the P/F ratio
To measure total lung capacity
To determine sleep stages

questions.text: Which bronchoscopy sampling method is listed for suspected pneumonia when expectorated samples are nondiagnostic?

answers.text: Bronchoalveolar lavage
Polysomnogram
Sniff test
Tensilon test

questions.text: Tuberculosis is caused by which organism?

answers.text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Staphylococcus aureus
Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Aspergillus

questions.text: Which finding best matches latent tuberculosis in the source?

answers.text: No symptoms, not infectious, positive PPD and IGRA, AFB negative
Symptomatic, infectious, and always AFB positive
Negative PPD, negative IGRA, and abnormal imaging
Only GI symptoms with no respiratory findings

questions.text: Which infection control setup is required for suspected or confirmed hospitalized TB?

answers.text: Private negative-pressure room with N95 mask for room entry
Routine room with no respiratory protection
Open bay room with surgical mask for staff only
Positive-pressure room with no mask requirement
